'''Enrico D'Ovidio''' (1843–1933) was an Italian [[mathematician]] who is known by his works on [[geometry]].

== Life and work ==
D'Ovidio, son of [[Liberalism|liberal]] parents involved in the Italian independence movement, studied at the [[University of Naples]] under his uncle, [[Achille Sannia]], who prepared him to enter in the School of Bridges and Roads. In 1869, he published with Sannia a very successful textbook to teach geometry in the schools.{{sfn | Kennedy | 1980 | p=176 }}

Encouraged by [[Eugenio Beltrami]], he obtained the chair on Algebra and Analytic Geometry at the [[University of Turin]] in 1872, and he remained there for the remaining 46 years of his life. He was also rector of the university from 1880 to 1885.{{sfn | Chang | 2011 | p=297 }}

The research of D'Ovidio was mainly in geometry and the most important works were produced when he was in Turin.{{sfn | Bastai Prat | 1992 | p=Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani }} Specially interesting is his work ''[https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01444650?LI=true Le funzioni metriche fondamentali negli spazi di quante si vogliono dimensioni e di curvatura costante] (The fundamental metrical functions in the n-dimensional spaces of constant curvature)'', published in 1876 and where he stated for first time the [[law of sines]] in n-dimensional curved spaces.{{sfn | Eriksson | 1978 | p=71 }}
